stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: When an earthquake occurs, it sends out two main kinds of body waves. Compressional P waves travel faster than shearing S waves, so the delay between their arrivals at a seismometer grows steadily with distance from the source. ______ a seismologist who measures that delay at three widely separated stations can calculate three distances and pinpoint where the rupture began.
explanation: The sentence before sets up a rule: the delay between P and S waves grows with distance. The sentence after says what that rule makes possible: measuring the delay at three stations locates the source. The second sentence follows from the first, so this is cause and effect, and "Consequently" signals that.

A.why: You picked a contrast word, but nothing in the second sentence goes against the first. Locating the rupture depends on the rule about growing delays. It doesn't push back on it.

C.why: You treated the second sentence as an example of the first. The first sentence describes how the waves behave, and the second describes a method that uses that behavior. A method built on a principle is a result of the principle, not one case of it.

D.why: You chose a same-direction word that means 'in the same way.' The second sentence doesn't describe a second, parallel thing that happens in a similar way. It describes what the first fact allows scientists to do.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Hydrologists have long credited floodplain wetlands with filtering sediment and nutrients from river water before it reaches downstream lakes. A survey of wetlands along one Midwestern river found that they also store floodwater, holding back as much as a tenth of peak flow during spring storms. ______ some of that stored water seeps downward into the aquifer beneath the floodplain, keeping nearby wells supplied long after the river has fallen.
explanation: The passage lists benefits that wetlands provide: filtering, then flood storage. The last sentence adds a third benefit, recharging groundwater. You can put 'and also' between the last two sentences and it still reads correctly, so the relationship is addition, and "Additionally" is the answer.

A.why: You treated the last sentence as a restatement. Refilling an aquifer is a new effect. It doesn't say 'holding back peak flow' in different words.

B.why: The recharge finding may be surprising, but surprising isn't the same as disagreeing. Nothing about the recharge contradicts the flood storage, so a contrast word like this one doesn't fit.

D.why: "Instead" means one thing replaces another. The water doesn't seep into the aquifer in place of being stored. It seeps down because it was stored, so the two facts work together.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Researchers documenting a dialect spoken in a single mountain valley found that it differs from neighboring dialects in only one grammatical respect. ______ every verb in the valley dialect carries a suffix showing whether the speaker saw the event personally or heard about it from someone else, a distinction the surrounding dialects leave unmarked.
explanation: The first sentence says there is exactly one grammatical difference. The second sentence tells you what that one difference is. When a sentence names the whole thing more precisely, you need a specification word, and "Specifically" is one.

A.why: "For example" introduces one item from a larger group. The passage says there is only one difference, so there is no group to take a sample from. The second sentence isn't an example of the difference. It is the difference.

B.why: "Similarly" links two separate things that resemble each other. The second sentence doesn't describe something parallel to the first. It describes the same difference in more detail.

D.why: You picked a contrast word, but the second sentence backs up the first. The difference it describes is the one the first sentence said existed.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Many coaches still open sprint practice with long static stretches, holding each position for a minute or more. Studies of trained sprinters suggest that the habit carries a cost: holds longer than sixty seconds temporarily reduce the force a stretched muscle can produce. ______ brief holds of under thirty seconds appear to have little measurable effect, but few traditional warm-up routines keep stretches that short.
explanation: The last sentence first grants a point against the passage's warning (short holds seem harmless), then turns back with "but" (few routines actually use short holds). Granting a point before disagreeing is concession, and the "but" later in the sentence confirms it. "Admittedly" is a concession word.

A.why: You read the last sentence as a result of the one before it. The finding that long holds reduce force doesn't lead to the conclusion that short holds are harmless. That is a separate finding, and it slightly weakens the passage's warning instead of following from it.

B.why: You treated short holds as an instance of the cost from the sentence before. But short holds are the case where the cost mostly disappears, so they can't be an example of it.

C.why: "Likewise" means the next point works the same way as the last one. Long holds reduce force, but short holds have little effect, so the two don't match. A same-direction word gets the relationship wrong.
